question: Single-cell blocks showed that no individual nucleator is needed for its neighbouring recruit. But the drive is the tissue's own field, so the nucleators could still cause the recruits collectively, at range. Does blocking the whole set of nucleators at once stop the recruits?
registeredBefore: any aggregate-block run existed; the runner and analysis are written after this file is committed
model: 1888, 11x11, hold 301, trained orders 0-3 code, scored moment 2173

definitions.nucleators: interior cells whose darkening after iteration 1200 had zero dark neighbours at the moment of crossing, in the untouched run
definitions.recruits: interior cells whose darkening after iteration 1200 had at least one dark neighbour, excluding any cell that is also a nucleator
definitions.block: G_pol held at 1.25 for iterations 1250-2173, the value already used in the single-cell test: inside the latching window for every neighbourhood, so the cell cannot be forced dark
definitions.survives: the cell is dark at iteration 2173 by the same Vmem cut the single-cell intervention used

conditions: ladder: the first k nucleators by crossing time, k = 2, 4, 6, 8, and all
randomControl: the same number of cells as allNucleators, drawn from interior cells that are dark at some point after 1200 but are not nucleators, 20 independent draws, seed 101
noop: every nucleator held at its own recorded conductance

P1.claim: the nucleators are collectively necessary for the recruits
P1.criterion: under allNucleators, at most half of the recruit cells that are dark at 2173 in the untouched run are still dark
P1.decides: if it fails, the recruits do not need the nucleators even in aggregate

P2.claim: the effect is graded, not all-or-nothing
P2.criterion: the number of surviving recruits falls monotonically with k across the ladder, Spearman rho <= -0.8 at p < 0.05

P3.claim: it is the nucleators specifically, not just the loss of eleven dark cells
P3.criterion: allNucleators leaves strictly fewer recruits dark than the median of the 20 random draws, and outside their 10th-90th percentile range

P4.claim: the route is the drive itself
P4.criterion: under allNucleators the mean G over the recruit cells at the untouched run's second peak (1765) is lower than baseline by more than 0.02, while the no-op control differs by less than 0.001

P5.criterion: the no-op condition changes no interior cell's state at 2173

notes: P1 and P3 are the load-bearing pair: P1 alone could be satisfied by any large perturbation, which is what P3 controls for. A failure of P1 together with the earlier per-link result would say the nucleator/recruit ordering is not causal at any scale.
